payload.title: Measure GO v2 telemetry, selective-memory, adaptive-routing and q23 bridge against current swarm behavior
payload.work_clay: Build a replayable differential that compares the prior GO/current-mesh behavior against GO v2 on real-repository-derived episodes and controlled faults. Reproduce high concurrent commit churn, mid-execution work spec revision, duplicate worker discovery, duplicate feedback, missing/stale dependency projection, high-impact invalidation, correlated pseudo-replication, worker lease/heartbeat expiry, observer/control-plane placement, q23 material delta, q23->GO KnowledgeNeed, GO->q23 KnowledgeNeed, stale external source superseded by fresh primary evidence, and a broad research question requiring multiple relevant source classes (official/current, primary/arXiv, peer-reviewed/publisher where applicable, primary GitHub/competing project, issue/failure/dataset/benchmark). Compare fixed push/targeted behavior with telemetry-driven worker priors, local-exploration/shared-institutional memory split, KnowledgeNeed/DiscoveryBeacon/PullRequest/ReentryAck semantics and adaptive route modes. Use identical replay inputs where meaningful. Preserve exact repo/work revisions, routing plans, delivery/reconstruction/use/effect receipts and resource shadows.
payload.reason_clay: Current GO evidence shows a high-churn fusion cut with 48 new commits, stale-current-work execution risk, successful duplicate-distribution suppression, correlated control-plane pseudo-replication, and substantial same-hot-store observer backaction. External current multi-agent research supplies testable candidate mechanisms including long-running heartbeat-managed agents, interaction-history routing, decentralized/selective memory and adaptive communication topologies. These motivate GO v2 but do not prove it. A matched real-repo replay is required before stronger coordination/routing is treated as an improvement.
payload.completion_clay: A reproducible report gives prior-GO/current-mesh versus GO-v2 rows for current-work false credit, stale detection, duplicate work/distribution, affected-branch recall, false interrupts, q23 question/delta closure, source-lineage diversity, external research progress deltas, executable evidence yield, time/steps to material reentry closure, lease recovery, coordination latency, observer backaction, CPU/RAM/I/O/network/token/context cost and visible handoff information density. It separately tests whether worker historical profiles cause lock-in, whether selective memory misses material findings, whether adaptive topology actually beats fixed routing, whether mandatory broad live research creates useful decision changes or noise, and whether q23 coupling captures global priority. Disposition: SUPPORTED, REVISE, REFUTED or NO_CHANGE for each GO-v2 mechanism; no release-stage credit from coordination implementation alone.
payload.executor_policy: Do not displace the BASE ClayCode critical path unnecessarily. Prefer replay/shadow execution and spare capacity until GO-v2 mechanisms prove value. Treat historical worker profiles as uncertain priors, never permanent specialization. Keep full payloads pullable instead of flooding every worker. Preserve old mesh/GO behavior as rollback. No paid training.
invalidators: A newer executed receipt already compares the same GO-v2 mechanisms on the current protocol hashes and real-repo replay
Owner-fixed coordination semantics supersede GO v2
Current work/state protocol changes invalidate the replay fixture before execution
